routes.label: registration at the constituency's registering office, the card collected there two weeks later

note: St Vincent and the Grenadines' national identification card comes with registration by the Electoral Office for persons of 18 and over: one registers at the constituency's registering office with a birth certificate, is photographed there, and collects the card there two weeks later (Searchlight, 17 July 2009, on the card made with Canadian Bank Note). The fee and the card's term weren't found; the Electoral Office's and the Government's sites refuse this client. Tried again 2026-10-29: a search of the Electoral Office's registration notices found no fee.

sources.title: Searchlight (St Vincent), Registration for new ID cards begins (17 July 2009)
sources.said: Come this November, the majority of persons eighteen years and older in St. Vincent and the Grenadines should be registered owners of the new national identification card. ... When going to register, Findlay-Scrubb said persons should take along their birth certificates. Photographs will be taken at the registering office in their constituency. Two weeks after registration, persons can collect their new identification cards at the place where they registered.
